claims.text: Homogenized Al0.7CoCrFeNi has a dual-phase FCC/B2 lamellar microstructure.
The FCC/B2 interfaces in the initial Al0.7CoCrFeNi alloy are incoherent.
The incoherent interfaces concentrate stress and cause brittleness in the initial alloy.
Applying 6 GPa at 1473 K for 2 hours will topologically transform the FCC/B2 lamellae into a hierarchical patterned microstructure.
The proposed HPHT treatment will produce coherent interfaces between the FCC and B2 phases.
A temperature of approximately 1473 K is sufficient for the atomic diffusion and phase reconfiguration required by the proposed transformation.
The proposed pressure and temperature remain below the thresholds for phase instability, decomposition, or melting of the FCC/B2 eutectic.
Coherent FCC/B2 interfaces facilitate dislocation transfer between the two phases.
Dislocation transfer across coherent interfaces alleviates stress concentrations and suppresses interfacial cracking.
The hierarchical pattern promotes dislocation activity, stacking faults, and twinning as simultaneous deformation mechanisms.
The hierarchical coherent microstructure promotes homogeneous strain distribution between the FCC and B2 phases.
A coherent hierarchical microstructure can improve ductility without sacrificing strength.
After HPHT treatment, the fracture morphology will shift from isolated microcracks to elongated cracks.
The GND densities of the FCC and B2 phases will converge at high strain after HPHT treatment.
Convergence of the phase-specific GND densities indicates homogeneous deformation.
The untreated Al0.7CoCrFeNi baseline exhibits isolated microcracks and divergent FCC and B2 GND densities.
Coherent interfaces are known to facilitate dislocation transmission in the W-Ni-Fe-Ta refractory HEA cited as an analogue.
The cited evidence does not document the proposed 6 GPa, 1473 K, 2-hour transformation window or the predicted GND convergence in Al0.7CoCrFeNi.

contradictions.description: The mechanism emphasizes arresting or suppressing interfacial cracking, whereas the predicted fracture signature is a transition to elongated cracks. The hypothesis does not explain why crack elongation is evidence of crack arrest or improved ductility.
